Please observe the peaceful village situation, because several dozen armed soldiers had arrived to improve it.

There was one open field in front. In this field the soldiers stood in matching military dress, same formation, rifles in hand and army swords also provided. For distance they had bullet. For closeness they had blade. Thus every geographical possibility had been considered.

Their fighting spirit was extremely present. Their voices were extremely absent. Not one man spoke. The setting sun had gone red behind them, laying the same colour over uniform and steel and making an already sinister gathering look fully confirmed.

At the front stood warriors in thick iron armour with very long swords. Behind them were several dozen ordinary soldiers. But do not count wrongly. One armoured fellow may have more fighting power than the whole quantity behind him. Mathematics will object, naturally. Mathematics has not seen his sword.

Then the foremost warrior shouted toward the village. Was he commander? Arre, listen only to the manner. A subordinate may be arrogant for himself. This man was arrogant for the entire unit. His rank came out of his mouth before the message.

The threat came again. Same meaning, stronger pronunciation: every soldier raised his rifle toward the village.

The whispers stopped. A wave of fear passed through the crowd, and still the hostility did not break. They stared back with complete bad intention.

Silent intent to kill.
Silent dushmani.

Then the balance broke—but not because anybody fired. One breath before the order could come, something moved at the rear of the crowd.

The human wall opened in alarm. Somebody was coming forward from inside it.

—Nahin!
—Go back, samurai-saab!
—Don't go, they'll kill you!
—Samurai-saab!

Voices pulled at him from every side. The man answered the whole village once.

en.html:
He stepped out before the military formation.

He too was an armoured warrior, same kind as the men threatening the village. Only his armour had learned a different life. Theirs was maintained: every plate secure, every mechanism ready. His damage remained where it happened, and whatever had worn down was continuing its journey downward.

Sometimes this is the full visible distance between regular soldier and fallen wanderer. One man has an army behind his armour. The other man has only the portions still functioning.

He moved forward again. A small hand caught his.

A little girl held on without speaking. He looked down, said nothing, and gently stroked her head. Then he loosened her fingers one by one.

Her eyes filled. He turned and continued walking.

Several soldiers prepared to rush out and seize him. Their commander stopped them with one hand, then advanced alone to meet him.

fallen wanderer"...What are you planning, Saginuma?"
unit commander"I am showing respect to my old commanding officer, Major Kakimi—former Major."
fallen wanderer"You will spare the village. Zubaan pakki?"
unit commander"If you are handed over, the village will answer for no crime. Jo bola, wahi hoga."
fallen wanderer"Good. But you truly mean to fight me alone? Why bring the whole baraat behind you?"
unit commander"One neck, one sword. If all men come together, there will be crowding."
fallen wanderer"..."
unit commander"You were very proud that nobody defeated you in single combat. I cannot send you to hell holding that pride in both hands. Rakho neeche. It does not belong to dead traitors."
fallen wanderer"...Achchha."
unit commander"Your wing-cloak is so badly torn that twin-wheel mounting is impossible. We fight on the ground. I will not defeat half a man and then spend whole night explaining the fraction."

unit commander"The head is mine, Kakimi. Tonight I shall drink well with your wrinkled neck for company."

en.html:
Both men knew how they would attack. Neither moved.

Each had prepared a perfect answer, and each knew the other fellow had not arrived empty-headed.

If Saginuma thrust, Kakimi would twist aside and cut him down before recovery.

If Kakimi cut first, Saginuma would step back, let the blade pass, then spring forward and put the point inside him.

Attack kills. Answer also kills. Excellent preparation had therefore manufactured complete paralysis.

Now the duel became a contest of stamina and concentration. Each man had to hold killing distance, preserve his stance, and catch the smallest change in the enemy. Imagine two fellows crossing one rope over a ravine, coming from opposite sides, and both have thoughtfully brought scissors.

Eventually one body would weaken. One guard would break. If the other man still possessed even a little strength, he would strike the opening and become victor.

Commander Saginuma. Fallen warrior Kakimi.

The roles were ready. Only death had not yet announced the casting.

At last the difference in age began showing its small dirty work.

Saginuma was in the full strength of middle years. Kakimi was only somewhat older, but old age had already taken his address and was walking there. The gap in stamina was small. Very good. Death also requires only one small gap.

Understand the fraud of this deadlock. From outside both men stood still, therefore both appeared to perform equal work. Inside, every moment cost Kakimi more. One breath became difficult, one muscle became late, and then the neck would open.

So Kakimi had to attack first with everything and kill Saginuma. This was his only remaining plan, and it was a very useless only remaining plan. Saginuma had ignored his own soldiers and come alone for this duel; you think such a fellow becomes careless now? He watched his former superior, present rebel, and gave him not one grain of opening.

Kakimi rushes, Saginuma stops him. Saginuma answers, Kakimi dies.

Thus Kakimi possessed two roads. Advance and die. Do not advance and die without travelling.

Still the scene lay calm like lake water. No wave, no splash. Under the surface, victory had moved toward one man and defeat toward the other. Honour and ruin were settling beside them. Only the bodies had not moved yet.

Machetes, hoes, hand axes—whatever could be pulled from the sheds. Villagers hid behind walls and struck careless soldiers from behind. It was not much of a counterattack.

A hunter brought out an old long gun and became more dangerous. He changed position with practiced care, waited for clean chances, and killed one soldier at a time.

Each shocked face that fell made something inside him happier and less sane. Kill more. They had killed this many; he would return the number. His anger wanted exact counting even after the world had stopped being exact.

This wish would not be fulfilled. Something had already taken aim at him, and it did not care how frightening he appeared to men on the ground.

Years of experience kept the hunter outside every soldier's sight. Nobody below could see him.

The armoured warrior's sudden slash split the hunter from top to bottom. The force remaining after this already unreasonable act blew apart the shed that had concealed him and tore a deep crack through the ground.

Can an ordinary human do such a thing? No. A warrior flying through the sky inside armour is already refusing the category of ordinary human.

The armour gave strength beyond the human domain. For practical purposes, these warriors were demons. Philosophers may submit a more precise category after surviving them.

Until then, the others had watched the foot soldiers work. Once one rider descended, the rest followed. Their violence made the soldiers' cruelty feel like a mild early-spring breeze.

The man did not look trained, yet every shot found its target. Four bullets flew toward four armoured warriors.

A miracle, and an entirely useless one.

One warrior tilted his head and let the bullet pass. One cut his bullet aside. One caught his in a bare hand. The fourth fellow did nothing.

The round struck his abdomen, left no mark, and fell. Even the bullet appeared to understand it had entered the wrong profession.

All four handled supersonic bullets the way a man handles flies.

He forced a path through the crowd. Ahead was the road to the neighbouring village. Keep running and he reaches it. Reach it and he lives.

People were forced to imitate caterpillars. Between them, here and there, others died in something resembling a human manner—if that is the word.

Their fates arrived exactly as the commander had ordered. Their own decisions meant nothing. Run, fight, invent plan, stand frozen: the armoured victors did not care. Only one side's will was permitted to become reality.

This was tyranny in pure form.

en.html:
The little girl whose ankle had been cut wondered why.

Until yesterday she had lived an ordinary village life. Her father worked in the mountains cutting timber. Her mother managed the household. She played with friends and sometimes helped at home. The days repeated. Nothing changed.

Then everything broke at once.

Why had the army come and destroyed the village? Her teacher said bad deeds returned to the person who committed them. Hurt someone, and hurt would come back.

Had she hurt someone? Had her father or mother? Had all the dead people? Had the friends now lying beside her with their legs cut?

Was it wrong to shelter Kakimi, to give him food and a place to sleep? He had been kind. Every adult called him an honourable samurai.

Or was there some other reason nobody had explained?

足首を切られた童女は思う。
　
　――なぜだろう。

　昨日までは村で普通に暮らしていた。

　父は山に入って木を切り出す林業に携わり、
　母は家の一切を取り仕切り、
　自分は友達と遊びつつ、時折母の手伝いをした。

　繰り返しの日々。
　何も変わらない毎日。

　それが唐突に壊される……
　どんな理由で、そんなことが起こるのだろう。

　あの軍隊というものがやって来て、村を滅茶滅茶に
してしまったのは、なんでだろう。

　学校の先生は教えてくれた。
　悪いことをすると自分に返ってくるのです。誰かに
酷いことをすれば自分も酷い目にあってしまいますよ、
と。

　自分は誰かに酷いことをしたのだろうか。
　父や母は。他にも大勢の死んだ人々は。今、自分と
一緒に足を切られて転がっている仲間達は。

　あの垣見という人を村に迎えて、寝床や食物を世話
したのが悪いことだったのだろうか。
　優しい人だったのに。大人もみんな、あんな立派な
お武家さまはいないと言っていたのに。

　それともほかの何かだろうか。

en.html:
If they were suffering because they had done something wrong, then what about the soldiers doing this?

Would the same punishment return to them? It had to. Otherwise the lesson was broken.

The army could destroy the village. Who could destroy the army? Who was strong enough to punish these armoured men?

Perhaps nobody.

Then punishment ended here. Children who did not even know their crime received everything; men visibly committing evil received nothing, because nobody had the strength to deliver it.

That was wrong. Bilkul wrong.

Amid destruction and screams, the girl who could no longer stand cried out inside herself.

Someone. Anyone. She would not even ask to be saved. Only: do not let the chain end with us.

Punish them too. Return what they have done. Give them this pain, this sorrow.

Somebody. God. Please.

She prayed with the grief of someone robbed and the pure anger of a child whose rulebook had caught the world cheating.

Make it right. This cannot be the correct arrangement.

何か酷いことをしたから、こんな目にあうのか。
　
　なら、<ruby>これ<rt>・・</rt></ruby>をした連中は？

　この連中も、いずれ同じ目にあうのだろうか。
　そうでなくては、おかしい。筋道が通らない。

　でも、誰が？

　村は軍隊の圧倒的な力で滅茶滅茶にされた。
　けど、軍隊は誰が滅茶滅茶にしてくれるのだろう。

　誰にそんなことができるのだろう。
　誰がこの、鎧の人々を罰せられるのだろう。

　誰もいないのではないか。

　誰もいないのなら。
　罰の連鎖はここで終わり。

　どんな悪いことをしたのかもわからない自分達だけ
が罰を受けて、確かに酷いことをしたこの連中は何の
報いも受けない。
　だって、誰も彼らを罰することができないのだから。

　おかしい。
　おかしいよ。

　破壊と悲鳴の楽奏の中、立てない童女は叫ぶ。
　
　――こんなの、おかしいよ。

　誰か。誰か。
　助けてとは言いません。
　お願い。<ruby>わたしたちで終わらせないで<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　あいつらにも罰を。
　悪いことをした報いを。
　同じ苦痛と悲しみを。

　誰か、与えてください。
　神様。
　お願いです。

　童女は祈る。
　奪われた者の嘆き、純粋な怒りを胸に。

　お願いします。
　こんなことは間違っているのだから。
　どうか、正しくしてください。

Laugh. Sing. Clap your hands. Dance with joy until joy cannot remember who started it.

Cast away the human. Live as one life, bas—nothing added.

Then existence fills with delight and sorrow becomes unnecessary.

Impossible? No. Anyone can do it.

You believe you cannot because you have forgotten the first and simplest fact: life exists to celebrate life.

A song could be heard.

The girl understood that she had misunderstood.

Ah. Is that how it is, God?

She listened to the song of life.

Living was not divided into good and evil? That was not what it meant?

The song taught her: where life lives, there is no crime and no punishment. Life needs only to remain pure as life. That is the correct arrangement.

The girl sang. She sang life. She sang joy.

Ah! We only had to be life with our whole hearts. We only had to pursue the one act called living.

Simply live. As creature, as life—honest, pure—

en.html:
Two meteors ran across heaven, crossed, turned, and crossed again. One collision had not settled the matter, so both returned with increased confidence.

The red star moved like a starving wolf.
The silver star moved lightly, like a doe.

A roar struck the night. Laughter crossed it.

The warrior in red swung with the sound of grief. The warrior in silver received the blow softly as an embrace and guided it away. One fellow had brought anger, shame, frustration and sorrow in complete luggage. The other answered with joy, comfort, acceptance and delight. Each considered itself the correct solution.

Act Four.

Was the final act another duel, copying the first?

No. For a duel, both parties must at least be performing the same activity. This basic condition was no longer satisfied.

This was communion.

This was play between one graceless man and one elegant princess who handled his fury as though he had brought too much baggage and she, being very kind, would throw it from the sky for him.
